subtitle: When Spirit Took Up Steel: The Birth of Miri-Piri

panels.shot: low-angle, iconic medium-wide of Guru Hargobind framed between shrine and throne
panels.action: Guru Hargobind stands tall on the parikrama at Amritsar, one sword at each hip, Harmandir Sahib gleaming behind him in the sarovar mist and the newly raised Akal Takht rising opposite like a solemn fortress of faith.

dialogue.text: In the age after Guru Arjan’s martyrdom, Hargobind rose with two swords and raised the Akal Takht, wedding devotion to the duty of protecting justice.

i18n.hi: गुरु अर्जन की शहादत के बाद के दौर में हरगोबिंद ने दो तलवारें उठाईं, अकाल तख्त बनाया, भक्ति को न्याय की रखवाली से जोड़ा।

panels.shot: high, contemplative wide over Amritsar city and Harmandir Sahib in the distance
panels.action: A dawn view of early seventeenth-century Amritsar shows mud-brick houses and narrow lanes stretching to the shimmering Harmandir Sahib set in its sarovar, the golden light thin and still, as if the town holds its breath.

dialogue.text: The year was 1606. In the dusty plains of Panjab, Amritsar’s sacred pool held a deep new silence, for Guru Arjan had been killed under Mughal power.

i18n.hi: साल था 1606। पंजाब की धूल भरी धरती पर, अमृतसर के सरोवर पर गहरा सन्नाटा था — गुरु अर्जन मुगल हुक्म में शहीद हो चुके थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in toward the Harmandir Sahib from the parikrama level
panels.action: Pilgrims move softly along the white parikrama around the Harmandir Sahib; some sit with bowed heads, others gaze at the sanctum where the Adi Granth rests, yet the air feels heavy, grief turned inward.

dialogue.text: The Sikhs had seen their Guru tortured and executed in Lahore. The wound was fresh, the questions sharp: could a community of song and service survive an empire’s wrath?

i18n.hi: सिखों ने अपने गुरु को लाहौर में तड़पते और मारते देखा था। ज़ख्म ताज़ा था, सवाल चुभते थे: क्या सेवा और गीत का यह समाज साम्राज्य के कहर से बचेगा?

panels.action: Young Guru Hargobind sits cross-legged inside a modest hall, his face calm yet shadowed by grief, a simple turban wrapped around his head, behind him a few Sikh elders sit in respectful silence.

dialogue.text: Into this storm stepped Hargobind, son of Guru Arjan. Still a young man, he carried the weight of succession, memory of a father’s martyrdom, and the eyes of an anxious sangat upon him.

i18n.hi: इसी तूफ़ान में गुरु अर्जन के बेटे हरगोबिंद आगे आए। अभी जवान थे, पर सिर पर गुरुगद्दी, दिल में पिता की शहादत, और चिंतित संगत की नज़रें उन पर थीं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Hargobind’s steady eyes
panels.action: Guru Hargobind’s eyes look straight ahead, clear and unwavering, a reflection of the Harmandir Sahib’s quiet waters visible in his pupils.

dialogue.text: Tradition remembers how he listened to Bhai Gurdas recite the Word, and then, with inward resolve, chose a new path where the rabab’s strings would stand beside drawn steel.

i18n.hi: रिवायत है, वे भाई गुरदास की बाणी सुनते रहे, फिर भीतर से ठान ली नई राह — जहाँ रबाब की तान के साथ नंगी तलवार भी खड़ी होगी।

panels.action: In a simple but solemn gathering, Guru Hargobind rises from a low platform while a senior Sikh fastens a broad belt around his waist, two scabbards hanging ready; the small crowd watches, uncertain and awed.

dialogue.text: On the day of his investiture as Guru, Hargobind did something unseen among the Gurus before him. At his waist, he girded not one, but two swords.

i18n.hi: गुरुगद्दी के दिन हरगोबिंद ने कुछ ऐसा किया जो पहले किसी गुरु ने न किया था। अपनी कमर पर उन्होंने एक नहीं, दो तलवारें बाँधीं।

panels.shot: low-angle, three-quarter view highlighting the swords
panels.action: The image lingers on Guru Hargobind standing upright, one sword resting on each hip, the plain steel glinting, his posture relaxed but unyielding, courtyards of Amritsar’s Guru-ka-Chakk behind him.

dialogue.text: One, he declared, was for piri, the sovereignty of the spirit. The other was for miri, the duty of worldly protection. Prayer would not retreat from the world; it would stand guard within it.

i18n.hi: एक, बोले, पीरी के लिए — रूहानी बादशाहत। दूसरी, मीरी के लिए — ज़मीनी रक्षा का फर्ज़। अब अरदास दुनिया से भागेगी नहीं, दुनिया के बीच पहरा देगी।

panels.shot: medium shot among gathered Sikhs, slightly over-the-shoulder from the sangat
panels.action: Guru Hargobind addresses a semi-circle of Sikhs in an open courtyard, some peasants, some artisans, a few in simple arms; he speaks with one hand resting lightly on a sword-hilt.

dialogue.speaker: guru_hargobind
dialogue.text: The Guru’s house will now feed the hungry and face the tyrant.

i18n.hi: अब गुरु का घर भूखे को भी खिलाएगा, ज़ालिम से भी टकराएगा।

panels.shot: wide shot on the parikrama, facing both Harmandir Sahib and the site of the future Akal Takht
panels.action: On the marble walkway around the sarovar, Guru Hargobind stands between the Harmandir Sahib on one side and an open space on the other, as if envisioning something yet to rise there; a faint breeze ruffles the water.

dialogue.text: But symbols alone were not enough. Across from the Harmandir Sahib’s low, humble sanctum, Hargobind imagined a second focus—a seat where the community’s temporal voice could speak.

i18n.hi: पर सिर्फ निशान काफी नहीं थे। हरमंदिर साहिब के विनम्र सरोवर के सामने हरगोबिंद ने दूसरा केन्द्र सोचा — ऐसा आसन जहाँ कौम की दुनियावी आवाज़ बोले।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle as if from ground level of the construction site
panels.action: Guru Hargobind oversees the raising of a raised platform; carpenters lift heavy beams, masons stack stone, while the Guru himself helps steady a pillar, his robes dusted from the work.

dialogue.text: Under his direction, a lofty platform began to rise. Built by hands hardened in labour and softened in kirtan, it would be called the Akal Takht—the Throne of the Timeless One.

i18n.hi: उनके इशारे पर ऊँचा मंच उठने लगा। मेहनत से सख्त हुए और कीर्तन से नरम हाथों ने इसे बनाया; नाम पड़ा अकाल तख्त — कालरहित का तख्त।

panels.shot: wide, symmetrical frontal view of Harmandir Sahib and Akal Takht facing each other
panels.action: The completed Akal Takht stands across the sarovar from the Harmandir Sahib; between them, the water reflects both structures, pilgrims moving like small figures between these two poles.

dialogue.text: Now two centres faced each other. The Harmandir held the scripture and song. The Akal Takht would hear disputes, guide the Panth, and symbolize that the Guru’s house claimed both inward and outward life.

i18n.hi: अब दो केन्द्र आमने-सामने थे। हरमंदिर में ग्रंथ और कीर्तन। अकाल तख्त पर झगड़े सुने जाते, पंथ को दिशा मिलती, और दिखता कि गुरु का घर भीतर और बाहर — दोनों जीवन का हकदार है।

panels.shot: medium-wide of the Akal Takht dais from a low upward angle
panels.action: Guru Hargobind sits upon a simple but elevated seat on the Akal Takht, Sikhs standing respectfully below; some present petitions, others seek counsel, while armed attendants stand discreetly at the sides.

dialogue.text: Here, Hargobind listened to quarrels over land, protection, and honour. His hukamnamas went out from such spaces, binding scattered Sikhs to a shared discipline and a growing sense of a Khalsa-like commonwealth.

i18n.hi: यहीं हरगोबिंद ज़मीन, सुरक्षा और इज़्ज़त के झगड़े सुनते। यहीं से उनके हुकमनामे निकलते, बिखरे सिखों को एक नियम, एक उभरती खालसा-जैसी रियासत से जोड़ते।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot inside a hall, with scribes and messengers
panels.action: Within a modest chamber, Guru Hargobind dictates to a scribe who writes carefully on paper; around them, a few horsemen prepare to ride with sealed letters, their faces earnest.

dialogue.text: Early letters in his name—hukamnamas that scholars still study—show a Guru drawing his followers not just to worship, but to readiness, discipline, and a life willing to defend the weak.

i18n.hi: उनके नाम के शुरुआती खत — हुकमनामे जिन्हें आज विद्वान पढ़ते हैं — दिखाते हैं एक गुरु, जो संगत को सिर्फ भजन नहीं, बल्कि तैयारी, अनुशासन और कमज़ोरों की रक्षा पर बुलाते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Hargobind in light armour preparing to mount a horse
panels.action: Guru Hargobind, now slightly older, wears light armour over his robes, the two swords still at his hips, as he places a foot in the stirrup of a waiting horse in a dusty yard near Amritsar.

dialogue.text: Mughal suspicion of a martial Guru grew. Conflicts flared in the years ahead, and Hargobind would lead Sikhs in open battle, insisting that a saint could, when pressed, be a soldier.

i18n.hi: मुग़ल दरबार को यह योद्धा-गुरु खटकने लगा। आगे के सालों में झड़पें भड़कीं, और हरगोबिंद खुद मोर्चे पर उतरे, कहते हुए कि संत ज़रूरत पर सिपाही भी हो सकता है।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of Gwalior Fort on a hill, seen from below
panels.action: The massive walls and bastions of Gwalior Fort loom over the landscape, their stone faces stern, with small human figures, including a distant Guru Hargobind, being led through a gate by armed guards.

dialogue.text: Imperial strategy took another form. Guru Hargobind was confined for years in the high walls of Gwalior Fort, his absence testing the resolve of a Panth that had only just stood up to power.

i18n.hi: सल्तनत ने और चाल चली। गुरु हरगोबिंद को सालों ग्वालियर किले की ऊँची दीवारों में कैद रखा; उनका दूर होना उस पंथ की हिम्मत की कसौटी बना जो अभी–अभी ताकत के सामने खड़ा हुआ था।

panels.shot: quiet medium shot inside a fort courtyard
panels.action: Within the fort’s stone courtyard, Guru Hargobind sits under a small patch of sky, speaking calmly with weary fellow prisoners; his two swords are absent, but his bearing remains composed and hopeful.

dialogue.text: Later Sikh tradition cherished tales of how, when release finally came, others walked free alongside him—a memory of the Guru’s concern for more than his own chains, even if court records remain silent.

i18n.hi: बाद की सिख परंपरा ने यह कथा सँभाली कि जब रिहाई आई, तो कई और भी उनके साथ आज़ाद हुए — एक याद कि गुरु अपनी जंजीरों से ज्यादा दूसरों की कैद के लिए फिक्रमंद थे, चाहे दरबारी काग़ज़ चुप रहें।

panels.shot: wide shot of Guru Hargobind returning to Amritsar, with sangat gathered
panels.action: Guru Hargobind rides back toward Amritsar on horseback, the two swords once more at his side; men and women of the sangat line the road, hands folded, some weeping with relief as the city’s skyline emerges.

dialogue.text: When he returned, the community he had shaped was different. It had learned to organize, to take counsel at the Akal Takht, to think of itself as a people who prayed with one hand and guarded with the other.

i18n.hi: जब वे लौटे, तो उनकी गढ़ी संगत बदल चुकी थी। उसने संगठित होना सीखा, अकाल तख्त पर मिल-बैठकर मशविरा करना सीखा, और खुद को ऐसी कौम माना जो एक हाथ से प्रार्थना करे, दूसरे से पहरा दे।

panels.shot: serene twilight wide shot of Harmandir Sahib and Akal Takht with silhouettes
panels.action: At twilight, Guru Hargobind stands again between the Harmandir Sahib and the Akal Takht, silhouetted; lamps glow in both buildings, their reflections trembling together on the water’s darkening surface.

dialogue.text: The twin swords at his side were not ornaments, but a teaching: that devotion without courage leaves injustice unchallenged, and courage without devotion forgets why it fights. In their balance lay the future of the Panth.

i18n.hi: उनकी कमर की दो तलवारें गहना नहीं, सबक थीं: सिर्फ भक्ति हो, हिम्मत न हो, तो ज़ुल्म बेखौफ़ रहता; सिर्फ हिम्मत हो, भक्ति न हो, तो लड़ाई का मकसद खो जाता। इन दोनों के संतुलन में ही पंथ का कल था।

panels.shot: close-up on the hilts of the two swords resting at Hargobind’s waist
panels.action: The frame closes on the simple, worn hilts of Guru Hargobind’s two swords, his hand resting lightly upon them, as if in blessing rather than in threat.

dialogue.text: From Guru Hargobind’s two swords and the Akal Takht’s rise flowed a legacy, later called Khalsa, of a people who hold scripture in the heart, steel in the hand, and justice in both.

i18n.hi: गुरु हरगोबिंद की दो तलवारों और अकाल तख्त की नींव से वही विरासत बह निकली जिसे आगे चलकर खालसा कहा गया — ऐसी कौम, जो दिल में बाणी, हाथ में शमशीर और दोनों में न्याय रखती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Spirit Took Up Steel: The Birth of Miri-Piri
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब रूह ने थामी शमशीर: मीरी-पीरी का जन्म
